title: Momentum as food
food: Risk-adjusted momentum: each asset's lookback return divided by its own volatility. Only positive momentum feeds the plate.
hypothesis: Assets that have been rising feed the plate; tubes toward them thicken, so the blob leans into trends and rests in cash when nothing rises. It should beat equal-weight hold after costs.

notes.why: In training the best of 384 settings looked strong (Sharpe 1.3 to 1.8), but the median setting sat near zero. The winner was the luckiest setting, not a real edge. Out of sample it lost to hold in all four folds. On hourly bars of mega-cap stocks momentum reverses too often, and rebalancing 20 to 50 times a year pays away what is left.
notes.learned: One thing did work: drawdown fell from 23.7% to 15.8%, because the blob rests in cash when nothing is rising. Sitting out protected it, and also made it miss the rallies.
notes.next: Try the opposite (EXP-004, mean reversion as food) and keep only the part that worked (EXP-005, the blob as a risk guard).
